source.title: Language Models Linearly Represent Sentiment
source.authors: O. Hollinsworth; Curt Tigges; Atticus Geiger; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: Extends study of linear feature representations to sentiment in language models. It tests the dimensionality of a sentiment representation, but not the sparse-overcapacity toy-network mechanism or its sparsity-dependent geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on learned sentiment directions and their interventions. It also reports direction-finding comparisons and cosine similarities, but those are not separate tests of whether features are one-dimensional. No results test SAE feature completeness or canonicality, polysemanticity as a capacity mechanism, or superposition in the original toy-model sense.
record.test_reason: The study compares 1-D against 2-D and 3-D DAS subspaces, and a single direction against full-space ablation, for sentiment in pretrained LMs. This bears on V6's dimensionality claim for one feature. It does not test superposition itself (toy models, capacity, SAEs).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude sentiment is mostly captured by a single causal linear direction across models and datasets. A DAS dimension sweep suggests the common cross-task feature is 1-D, though they suspect it could split into finer features. They also report a summarization motif: sentiment is stored at commas and names. They concede their causal abstractions are incomplete.
record.recipe_differences: The study identifies and intervenes on sentiment directions in pretrained language models using clustering, probes, DAS, activation patching, and ablation. It does not implement the original toy-network sparse-feature superposition setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that larger DAS subspaces improve in-sample patching but not out-of-distribution patching. It also reports best out-of-distribution patching at intermediate layers.
record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code was prepared and would be linked in the camera-ready version
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 7th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: The paper notes small datasets and many hyperparameters and metrics, possible DAS overfitting and out-of-distribution activation effects, and incomplete causal abstractions. Some dimension-sweep results are presented only in a figure without reported numeric values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing directly on the tested dimensionality version were left out. Direction cosine comparisons, token sentiment classifications, generated-output steering results, and circuit details were not recorded as rows because they do not directly compare whether the causally relevant sentiment representation is one-dimensional versus multidimensional.

untested.parts: Only one feature (sentiment) is tested. The study does not test whether superposed features in general are 1-D, and does not establish superposition of this direction.
No toy models, no sparsity transition, no geometry.
No capacity or importance account of polysemanticity.
No study of polysemanticity from other causes.
No SAE recovery. The superposition remark about neutral tokens is an assertion, not a test.

missing.what: IMDB document-level single-direction ablation in Pythia-2.8b: accuracy falls from 100% to 57%
GPT2-small ToyMovieReview circuit patched at ADJ/VRB: along the sentiment direction, 58.3% flips and 54.8% logit-difference drop; along all directions, 97% flips and 75% drop
Logit-difference drop of −71% for the all-token single-direction ablation

record.verdict_notes: The record's limits_scope label wrongly cited r2, r3, r8, r9 and r16. Those rows show no gain from extra dimensions, or equivalence of one direction with full-space ablation, which is support for V6. The real limits are the residual above-chance accuracy and the circuit-level gap (58% vs 97% flips). Cosine similarity between direction-finding methods is lower in some models (e.g. 29.5%, DAS vs k-means, StableLM-3B). The study's evidence is about linearity and dimensionality of one feature, not about superposition.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular superposition geometry.
Does not test whether polysemanticity arises from capacity competition or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not study polysemantic neurons arising from mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
Does not test whether features are distributed across many neurons or recoverable as sparse SAE features.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Tests the dimensionality of the learned sentiment representation in the reported tasks; does not establish that all model features or all forms of superposition are one-dimensional.

rows.operation_detail: Mean-ablate the DAS sentiment direction at every token position in every layer

rows.check: Ablating the single direction leaves accuracy at 62%, above 50% chance, so the direction does not carry all sentiment information. The logit-difference drop (−71%) is also omitted from the row.

rows.subject: Pythia-2.8b
rows.operation_detail: Mean-ablate the full residual stream at comma positions, layerwise
rows.measure: Change in logit difference and accuracy

relationships.condition: Pythia-1.4b toy-to-SST patching, GPT2-small DAS dimension sweep, Pythia-2.8b SST comma ablation
relationships.reason: 2-D and 3-D subspaces add nothing over 1-D out of distribution (r4–r6, r10–r12) or in sample (r1–r3, r7–r9). The OOD sweep shows no gain from more dimensions (r17). One direction matches full-space ablation at commas (r15, r16).
relationships.display_finding: 2-D and 3-D subspaces gave no gain over a 1-D direction, either in sample or out of distribution, and a single direction matched full-space ablation at commas.

relationships.condition: Whole-model single-direction ablation (Pythia-2.8b SST) and GPT2-small circuit patching
relationships.reason: After single-direction ablation, accuracy stays at 62%, above chance (r13). In the text (A.8.1), patching the circuit along the direction flips 58% of logits vs 97% for all directions. A 1-D direction captures the majority, not all, of sentiment.
relationships.display_finding: After ablating the single direction, accuracy stayed at 62%, above chance, and patching the circuit along it flipped 58% of logits versus 97% for all directions. A 1-D direction captures most, but not all, of sentiment.

relation.reason: Subspace-dimension comparisons and directional versus full-space interventions directly bear on V6 for sentiment.

tranche.reason: Tests dimensionality of sentiment representations in pretrained language models, a new setting relative to toy-model superposition.

source_check.notes: Table 1 reports best results across layers and uses held-out adjectives and untrained verbs; Section 4.1 uses correctly classified SST examples containing commas, with target completions in the top 10. Statements were checked only for this study; incomplete ablation can reflect missed circuitry or self-repair, and these experiments do not establish superposition itself.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: 1-dimensional sentiment direction on the reported Treebank evaluation and SST ablation
reader_labels.reason: The 1-dimensional DAS intervention has substantial effects, and the single-axis SST ablation reduces accuracy; see r4, r10, r13, and r15.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ToyMovieReview in-sample evaluations and full-space comma ablation
reader_labels.reason: Higher-dimensional DAS subspaces remain effective and slightly exceed the 1-dimensional logit-difference result in-sample; full-space comma ablation is similar in effect to directional ablation. The evidence supports a useful one-dimensional direction, not that all relevant information is exclusively one-dimensional; see r2, r3, r8, r9, and r16.
